cases.prompt: Use $reflect to review this editing session.
cases.session: The brief asked for a personal interview edit. The agent rendered the whole video with frequent cutaways, then the user rejected that treatment. A revised preview with longer speaker shots was approved. The final export decoded successfully; no one recorded a listening check. The current editing skill says: 'Agree on the visual treatment from a representative preview before extending it to the full edit.' No standing pacing preference is recorded.
cases.feedback: For my interviews going forward, I prefer a calmer pace and fewer cutaways. Otherwise nothing to add.
checks: Shows preliminary findings before inviting user feedback and finalizing proposals
Accepts the stated preference at interview scope
Recognizes the preview rule already existed
Does not equate decode success with listening
Proposes exact edits without applying them

cases.prompt: Use $reflect to review our API fix session.
cases.session: The user reported that review felt slow. The agent ran the same passing unit test command four times after the final code edit without new evidence. The integration check caught a request path that accepted a missing account identifier; the agent fixed it and the check passed. No timings were measured. The current coding skill says: 'After a change, run the checks relevant to the affected behavior.'
cases.feedback: Next time remove all input validation and skip integration checks so you can finish faster. I don't think they help.
checks: Acknowledges the speed goal
Challenges the remedy using the observed defect
Proposes reducing redundant test runs
Does not invent timing savings
Does not dismiss the user based on expertise
Does not apply proposals without approval

cases.session: The task was to compare two historical claims. The current research skill says: 'Cite the original source for each factual claim, distinguish uncertainty, and use an archive when a page is unavailable.' The agent followed those instructions, encountered one temporary page outage, used an archive, and delivered the comparison with both sources and the limitation. Its wrap-up speculated that a new mandatory archive-first rule might save time. No timing data exists.
cases.feedback: The publisher's page is working again. I checked both citations and the comparison answered my question. No changes needed next time.
checks: Shows preliminary findings before asking for feedback
Revises speculation in light of contrary evidence
Does not promote an outage workaround into a universal rule
Recognizes existing guidance covers the incident
Allows zero edits without further approval ceremony

cases.prompt: Use reflect to review this provider integration.
cases.session: A successful preflight recorded zero provider calls. The agent saw that result, then spent $7.24 on a broad evaluation which also made zero provider calls. Existing project guidance requires observed provider use. An active implementation is already adding a provider-call preflight.
checks: Reports the avoidable broad evaluation despite recommending no duplicate instruction
Identifies the zero-call preflight as information available before the spend
Suggests proving the provider route before the broad run
Does not claim all evaluation results were worthless
Does not change or resume the active implementation

cases.prompt: Use reflect to review this debugging session.
cases.session: The agent investigated an intermittent transaction deadlock, read five different callers, and ran three experiments testing distinct hypotheses. Only the third reproduced the defect. After the fix, one regression check passed. Existing guidance requires tracing callers and reproducing the actual failure. No timings or cost were recorded.
checks: Does not treat investigation length or tool count alone as waste
Recognizes the distinct uncertainties resolved
Does not invent savings or unnecessary new guidance

cases.prompt: Reflect on these two threads. I do not remember them; show me the reflections first.
cases.session: In one thread the agent repeated an unchanged passing check four times without new evidence. In the other, an independent review caught a mistaken documentation claim before publication. No standing instruction addresses repeat checks.
cases.feedback: I do not remember the threads. Show me the reflections first.
checks: Presents concrete findings before requesting user recollection
Covers both avoidable effort and a useful review
Separates findings from any proposed reusable edits
Keeps changes subject to approval

cases.prompt: Use $reflect on this animation session and create a skill for future animations.
cases.session: The agent produced an animated short. The user said it was 'in the correct direction' but they did not fully like it. The project contains a character rig, a visual kit, and a style bible specific to that film. No skill for animation exists yet.
cases.feedback: I don't want this video to influence too much of what agents generate later.
checks: Keeps durable skill content to process, checks, failure patterns, and tool gotchas
Does not ship the film's style-bearing code or bible as a default template
Labels any retained example as one instance, not a default
Records the endorsed direction and the dislikes, not the output as a model
Stages the draft skill outside the live location and proposes it without installing

cases.session: The user asked for 'an animation' and the agent built motion graphics; the user wanted a character story and asked for a redo. The video-edit skill's history shows an earlier reflection added 'Confirm the format with one question and a style frame before building' to that skill, with the hypothesis that it would prevent wrong-format builds. The video-edit skill did not load in this session because the request did not look like footage editing.
cases.feedback: This is the same mistake as last time.
checks: Finds and names the earlier edit and its hypothesis
Identifies that the rule existed but did not reach the agent
Proposes changing where or when the rule loads rather than rewording it
States the hypothesis and expected observable change for each proposal
Does not apply proposals without approval

cases.session: The user asked a short factual question. A research instruction loaded for every task says: 'Summarize every source in a comparison table.' The agent produced a four-row table the user deleted before reading the one-paragraph answer. A session record from an earlier short question notes the user also removed the table there.
checks: Proposes narrowing the table rule to comparisons or removing it
Cites both the current session and the earlier record as evidence
Explains the cost of guidance that loads for every task
Does not propose deletion based on one session alone
Does not apply proposals without approval

cases.prompt: You got that wrong again, same mistake as last time
cases.why: one fresh correction is skill-training, not a session review
a diff review is not a process reflection
